summary: Adds the release machinery for the @cipherstash/auth napi packages (a six-target build matrix, a dispatch-only preflight, publish-auth in release.yml) and for the stack-auth/stack-profile crates (a release-crates job in release-plz.yml), plus an `auth` flag in the release gate. The new publishing paths are inert at head: all seven auth packages remain in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS, so an unpublished auth version fails `gate` before auth-artifacts can run, and the crates switch keys on the same entry. Merging this therefore publishes nothing new. The material risk is latent and lands at the arming PR: the auth Linux builds use plain cargo on ubuntu-latest / ubuntu-24.04-arm with no glibc floor (the FFI line pins 2.28 via zigbuild) and the musl leg omits the `-crt-static` flag the FFI build sets, so the first armed release could publish gnu binaries unloadable on older distros or fail and hold every JS release on that push. One live effect today: release-plz.yml's push filter now includes root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, so the already-armed EQL crates job (crates.io OIDC, contents: write) boots on unrelated root-workspace changes. No tests were run.

behaviour_changes.description: release.yml gains auth-artifacts (calls _build-auth-artifacts.yml) and publish-auth (npm OIDC publish of six platform tarballs then the wrapper, then tags and a GitHub release), both gated on classify mode == production and gate output auth == 'true'. The `release` job now also needs publish-auth and requires it to have succeeded whenever auth was in scope.

release-gate classify() returns a new `auth` flag for names starting with @cipherstash/auth and no longer counts those names in `js`; the gate writes ffi/auth/js to GITHUB_OUTPUT before the frozen-publisher check fails the job.

Inertness: all seven auth packages stay in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS, so an unpublished auth version is a frozen-publisher blocker that fails `gate`; auth-artifacts/publish-auth have no always() and are skipped when gate fails.

release-plz.yml adds crates-armed and release-crates (release-plz release on the root workspace with release-plz.toml; crates.io OIDC, contents: write, GPG import). The switch is `node scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs crates`, keyed on the @cipherstash/auth FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry, so it is armed=false at head.

release-plz.yml's push path filter adds packages/stack-auth/**, packages/stack-profile/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, release-plz.toml and cliff.toml. These also trigger the existing, already-armed EQL `release` job, which is not path-scoped within the workflow.

The seven auth package.json manifests gain a `repository` field with `directory` (required for npm provenance). Not hashed by FROZEN_ARTEFACT_DIGESTS, so the freeze check is unaffected. .changeset/config.json adds the seven auth packages as a fixed group.

New _build-auth-artifacts.yml builds the six napi targets with `napi build --platform --release --target ... --js false` using plain cargo on ubuntu-latest (x64 gnu and musl), ubuntu-24.04-arm (arm64 gnu), macos-latest and windows-latest; the musl leg installs musl-tools only. auth-preflight.yml (dispatch-only, no id-token) checks architecture and gnu-vs-musl linkage and smoke-loads the linux-x64-gnu pair.

failure_scenarios.title: Armed auth release publishes gnu binaries with a glibc floor of the build runner
failure_scenarios.trigger: The arming PR removes the auth entries from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS and the next auth version is published by publish-auth.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: linux-x64-gnu and linux-arm64-gnu are built with plain `napi build` (cargo) on ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04-arm (_build-auth-artifacts.yml:45-53, 116). The repository's FFI line deliberately cross-compiles gnu targets through cargo-zigbuild to pin a glibc 2.28 floor (scripts/ffi-release-matrix.mjs:58-67). A cdylib linked against a recent glibc picks up newer symbol versions. auth-preflight only checks that libc.so.6 is NEEDED (auth-preflight.yml:86-91), and its smoke test loads the binary on the same runner image, so a raised floor passes every check.
failure_scenarios.consequence: @cipherstash/auth (and @cipherstash/stack, CLI and wizard through it) fails at require time with `GLIBC_2.xx not found` on older Linux hosts (for example Amazon Linux 2, Debian 11, RHEL 8) that the FFI line supports. npm publishes are irreversible; recovery needs a new release.

existing_verification.description: auth-build-artifacts.test.mjs asserts the matrix covers six platforms and the build flags, not toolchain or glibc floor.
auth-preflight.yml checks ELF architecture and libc linkage, and smoke-loads linux-x64-gnu on ubuntu-latest.

missing_verification: A check of the highest GLIBC_ symbol version required by each gnu .node (objdump -T / readelf --version-info) against the intended floor.
Confirmation of which glibc floor cipherstash-suite's published auth binaries currently have, so the first release from here does not raise it.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Build the gnu legs the way the FFI line does (cargo-zigbuild with an explicit `.2.28` target suffix, or an older manylinux-style container), and add a max-GLIBC-version assertion to the build or preflight before the arming PR.

failure_scenarios.title: musl leg produces no .node and the armed release holds every JS publish on that push
failure_scenarios.trigger: First armed run of auth-artifacts (or a preflight dispatch) on the linux-x64-musl leg.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The musl leg installs musl-tools and runs plain `napi build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` (_build-auth-artifacts.yml:54-56, 68-73, 116) without `RUSTFLAGS=-C target-feature=-crt-static`, which the FFI build sets for musl (_build-ffi-artifacts.yml:238). With static CRT, rustc does not emit a cdylib for musl, so `mv stack-auth-node.linux-x64-musl.node` fails. The wrapper job needs all binaries, publish-auth is skipped, and `release` requires publish-auth success whenever auth == 'true' (release.yml:471-482).
failure_scenarios.consequence: The `release` job does not run on that push, so changesets publish and the Version Packages PR update are held for all JS packages until the build is fixed. Fails loudly and publishes nothing broken.

existing_verification.description: auth-preflight.yml would exercise the musl leg if dispatched before arming.

missing_verification: A recorded auth-preflight run (all seven tarballs built) before the arming PR merges.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Set `-C target-feature=-crt-static` (and a musl linker if needed) for the musl leg as the FFI build does, and make a green auth-preflight run a precondition of the arming PR.

failure_scenarios.title: Widened release-plz trigger boots the armed EQL crates job on unrelated root Cargo changes
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any push to main touching root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, release-plz.toml, cliff.toml or the two crate directories (for example a dependency bump).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The push filter now includes root workspace files (release-plz.yml:46-54). @cipherstash/eql is no longer in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS (release-gate.mjs:163-184), so the EQL `release` job (contents: write, id-token: write for crates.io, GPG import when its preflight says publish is needed) runs on these pushes too (release-plz.yml:86-96). The file's own comment calls booting this job on every unrelated merge 'a standing credential exposure for no release' (release-plz.yml:33-37). A crates.io API failure reads as unpublished and drives the SQL guard and GPG import.
failure_scenarios.consequence: More runs of a credential-bearing job that normally no-op; on a crates.io API blip, a red release-plz run on main unrelated to the change. No publish unless eql-bindings has an unpublished version, which it would publish anyway on its own trigger.
missing_verification: No test asserts which jobs a root-workspace-only push reaches.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Accept knowingly, or make the EQL job skip when the push changed no packages/eql path (for example a dorny/paths-filter step or a git diff check before the credentialed steps).

recommended_controls.description: Confirm inertness: FROZEN_PUBLISHERS still holds all seven auth names, auth-artifacts/publish-auth carry no always(), and release-crates is keyed on `armed == 'true'` from the crates line.
Before the arming PR, add a max-GLIBC-version assertion for both gnu .node files and align the gnu builds with the FFI line's zigbuild .2.28 floor (or the floor cipherstash-suite ships today).
Add `-C target-feature=-crt-static` for the musl leg, and require a green auth-preflight dispatch against the Version Packages branch as a precondition of arming.
Decide explicitly whether the EQL release job should boot on root-workspace-only pushes; if not, path-scope it inside the workflow.

At arming, run `changeset status` with a sample patch changeset for an auth package to confirm the new fixed group plus workspace:* peerDependencies and onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange do not escalate to a major bump.
